enabled.description:
The switch. Off: no picture is kept, the power reel's items run as they always did, nothing is decided at login.
`lares session save | show | restore` work by hand either way.

Takes true or false. Default: false.

afterLogout.description:
After a LOG-OUT (the reel's item), at the next login of the same boot:
  "ask"           a toast with Restore / Discard, normal urgency, that stays until you answer it
  "ask-critical"  the same toast, critical
  "auto"          restored by itself (under the boot lock: the windows stand ready at the unlock)
  "off"           nothing

Takes "ask", "ask-critical", "auto" or "off". Default: "ask".

afterReboot.description:
After a REBOOT or POWER-OFF (the reel's items, or a shutdown from a terminal), and after a log-out followed by a
new boot: the same four words.

Takes "ask", "ask-critical", "auto" or "off". Default: "ask".

afterCrash.description:
After a session that did NOT end (a Hyprland crash, a kill, a power loss): "ask" (a critical, sticky toast; a restore
then runs no command by itself) or "off". Never restored by itself: what was open may be why it crashed.

Takes "ask" or "off". Default: "ask".

maxAgeHours.description:
A saved session older than this is not offered.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 168.

run.description:
A terminal's running program is RUN again by itself only when it is on the run list (tools/session/rules.json:
lazygit, nvim, btop, yazi, less, man, tail -f, journalctl -f, git log, claude --resume ... ) -- everything else is only
TYPED at the prompt and waits for Enter. Add programs you trust (any arguments), or force one to be typed:
e.g. ["k9s", "lazydocker", "cava"]

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

type.description:
e.g. ["nvim"]

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

launch.x-wants: a command as a list of texts, like ["kitty", "-e", "yazi"]

apps.description:
Per window class (as `hyprctl clients` names it):
  "launch"       the command that starts the app, instead of the one found (its .desktop entry, else its command line)
  "selfRestore"  true: the app reopens its own windows (a browser, an editor) -- it is started ONCE and its windows
                 are put back by their titles
  "slow"         true: its window may come minutes later (the Windows VM's viewer, built in: its launcher connects at
                 once to a VM that runs and boots one that does not). Never held back: it opens on its own
                 workspace whenever it comes
  "skip"         true: never started by a restore
  ("launch" is a list: ["code", "--new-window"]. "why" and "folders" are notes the tool itself reads.)

Default: {}.

skipClasses.description:
Classes never saved (added to the built-in ones: the shell's own windows, portal dialogs).

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

claude.description:
A Claude Code terminal in a restored session: "resume" (its conversation goes on) | "fresh" (a new one in the same folder) | "type" (the command is
typed and waits for Enter).

Takes "resume", "fresh" or "type". Default: "resume".

confirmReplace.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

presets.description: Desktop presets: the same for the terminals of a preset ("fresh" | "resume"), and whether a load that closes other windows asks first.

keep.description:
How many saved sessions are kept. 1 to 100.

Takes a whole number 1 .. 100. Default: 5.

resultToast.description:
The toast that closes a restore: "always" | "needs" (only when something needs you) | "off".

Takes "always", "needs" or "off". Default: "always".

windowTimeoutMs.description:
How long a restore waits for a terminal's window, and for an app's windows, before it reports them missing.

Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 10000.

appTimeoutMs.description: Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 30000.

closeTimeoutMs.description:
Presets (`lares session preset ...`, work whether "enabled" is true or not): loading one with --replace first closes the
windows the preset has no place for and waits this long for each to go. A window that asks first (unsaved changes)
stays open and is reported.

Takes a whole number, 0 and up. Default: 8000.
